title: Tokenization fingerprint and template compatibility guardrails for model bundles
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: During recent onboarding of community models we observed intermittent generation regressions and incorrect performance profile numbers caused by mismatches between tokenizer artifacts bundled with the model and the canonical chat templates used by consumers. Mismatches include: differing role delimiters, vocab ordering changes, and tokenizer config flags (e.g., byte-level vs. unicode normalization) not reflected in template heuristics. These lead to token count variance, prefix/KV cache misalignment, and noisy performance profiles being published.

Proposal: Implement a deterministic tokenization fingerprint and a preflight compatibility pipeline that gates profile publishing and model pinning until templates and tokenizer are compatible.

1) Tokenizer fingerprinting: compute a stable fingerprint for every tokenizer artifact we ingest consisting of the tokenizer type, version, normalized vocab hash, special token mapping hash, and key config flags. Store fingerprint as a single short string (e.g., tkfp:v0:<hex>) inside the model bundle metadata and the template set manifest.

2) Preflight checks during onboarding: extend the onboarding pipeline to compare tokenizer fingerprint against template manifest. If mismatch, mark onboarding as "template-incompatible" and prevent performance profile publish and model version pinning. Generate clear remediation suggestions.

3) Automated template normalization tool: provide a utility that attempts non-destructive fixes for common mismatches (normalize role delimiters, escape sequences, collapse repeated whitespace patterns, and align special tokens). Each normalization run creates a diff and a suggested template revision for review by PM/Documentation.

4) Tokenization smoke-tests: add a minimal set of canonical prompts used to validate token counts and token-boundary invariants across the tokenizer and normalized templates. Smoke-test passes are required before profile publish.

5) Telemetry and rollback: emit onboarding telemetry when a tokenizer-template mismatch occurs including model id, tokenizer fingerprint, template manifest hash, and failing smoke-test IDs. If a performance profile has already been published for a model with later-identified tokenizer regressions, automatically mark the profile as "suspect" and queue a re-eval.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fingerprint is computed and stored for new onboarding runs and visible in the model bundle metadata.
- Onboarding runs with mismatched fingerprints are blocked from publishing performance profiles and from automatic version pinning.
- Normalization tool can produce a suggested template revision for the top 3 mismatch classes and includes a conservative flag to avoid semantic changes.
- Smoke-tests run in CI for onboarding and surface deterministic token counts for canonical prompts.
- Relevant telemetry and a lightweight dashboard exist to triage tokenizer-template incompatibilities.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (week 1): implement fingerprint generation and add to onboarding metadata. Soft-fail (warn only) on mismatches and log telemetry.
- Phase 2 (week 2): add preflight gating to block profile publish; introduce normalization tool and human review flow.
- Phase 3 (week 3): require smoke-tests as part of onboarding CI; wire auto-marking of suspect profiles and provide remediation playbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives: conservative fingerprint composition (exclude irrelevant metadata) and a soft-fail rollout period.
- Breaking downstream tools that relied on non-normalized templates: provide a suggested-rewrite flow and 48h human review window before enforcement.
- Edge cases where normalization changes semantics: normalization tool must run with a --safe flag and output explicit diffs for human approval.

Open questions:
- Which exact tokenizer fields should be part of the fingerprint to balance sensitivity vs noise?
- Should we require a signed tokenizer binary for private deployments?
- How to version the fingerprint algorithm so older model bundles remain interpretable?

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenizer+Template+Fingerprint+Design
- PR (initial spike): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-inference/pull/12456
- Perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/onboarding/tokenizer-compat

Next steps:
- Spike fingerprint format and produce compatibility matrix for top 10 community tokenizers (owner: Ethan)
- Build normalization CLI and unit tests (owner: Sofia)
- Add smoke-test set and CI gating (owner: QA team)
